S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

symptom.disease_info: Schizophrenia is a chronic psychotic disorder characterized by distortions in thinking and perception (such as delusions and hallucinations), disorganized thought and behavior, and/or prominent negative symptoms like diminished emotional expression and avolition. It typically follows a course that includes a prodromal phase of subtle social and functional decline, an active phase of florid psychotic symptoms, and a residual phase where negative symptoms and cognitive deficits may predominate. Onset is most common in late adolescence or early adulthood, but late-onset cases can occur, especially in women, and the illness often leads to impairment in work, relationships, and self-care if untreated. It is distinguished from mood disorders with psychotic features by the persistence of psychotic symptoms outside of mood episodes, and from brief or substance-induced psychoses by its longer duration and characteristic pattern of deterioration.

patient.stressor: About two and a half years ago, Alicia led a high‑stakes merger that required long hours, frequent travel, and constant negotiation with investors, on top of her usual commitment to experimental art collaborations. Her normally productive, if somewhat chaotic, work style began to fray as she increasingly missed key calls, lost track of strategic documents, and withdrew from the gallery openings and yoga classes that had once kept her grounded. Colleagues initially assumed burnout, but over the following year her board grew alarmed by her erratic decision‑making, unexplained absences from critical meetings, and difficulty following through on basic executive tasks, which clashed sharply with her prior reputation. After a tense board review and a near loss of a major client, her spouse and the company’s HR director persuaded her to see a psychiatrist when it became clear that the degree of disorganization and detachment went far beyond stress or overwork.
patient.chief_complaint: “My team keeps telling me my behavior and decisions don’t make sense anymore, and I feel like I can’t control what I’m doing at work.”

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: In the past couple of years I’ve started hearing this man’s voice, very clear, like someone on a conference call without video, commenting on what I’m doing—telling me I’m making a mess of the company or that people are laughing at me—even when I’m alone in my apartment or in a quiet boardroom and I know there’s no one actually there talking.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: What scares me most is that at work I’ll suddenly find myself standing in the middle of the office just staring at the wall or pacing the hallway, laughing or snapping at people at completely wrong moments, or refusing to go into a meeting I scheduled because it suddenly feels dangerous, and later I can’t explain to anyone, including myself, why I acted that way or why I couldn’t just behave normally.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: These days I mostly sit on the couch or at my desk doing nothing for long stretches, ignoring calls from my team and even close friends, and I feel flat and blank—no real joy in the art projects I used to love, no drive to go to yoga or even shower sometimes—like the part of me that cared about anything just quietly shut off.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: Over the last couple of years I’ve gone from reliably running the company and my art projects to missing critical meetings, nearly losing a major client, and pulling away from friends and basic routines like regular hygiene, to the point that my spouse and board are questioning whether I can keep functioning in my role.
add_requirements.duration: Looking back, this overall slide in my thinking, motivation, and ability to function has been going on for a little over two years, starting around the time of that big merger project.
add_requirements.psychotic_symptoms_duration: The clear voice commenting on me and the really bizarre behavior at work have been a regular problem for roughly the last three months.
